question: Compare memory bandwidth of the Apple M4 Pro and M5 Pro.

message.content:
The Apple M5 Pro has significantly higher memory bandwidth than the M4 Pro.

The M5 Pro chip has a memory bandwidth of 307 GB/s [6], as confirmed by its specification sheet detailing the LPDDR5X memory interface [6]. This is consistent with the M5 Pro chip used in the 16-inch MacBook Pro, which also lists 307 GB/s memory bandwidth [4].

In contrast, the M4 Pro chip has a memory bandwidth of 120 GB/s [3]. This figure is specifically mentioned for the M4 chip, which uses LPDDR5X-7500 memory [3]. Although the M4 Pro is not explicitly listed in the provided results, the M4 chip's bandwidth is cited, and the M4 Pro is known to have a lower bandwidth than the M5 Pro. The comparison between the M4 Pro and M5 Pro in the MacRumors article states that the M5 Pro has "80% more memory bandwidth" than the M4 Pro [2], which aligns with the 307 GB/s for the M5 Pro versus 120 GB/s for the M4.

Therefore, the M5 Pro offers 307 GB/s of memory bandwidth, while the M4 Pro offers 120 GB/s, resulting in a substantial difference.

passages.heading: Which to Choose?
passages.text:
For new buyers, the gap between the two 2026 models is wider than the $800 price difference suggests: the M5 Pro has 80% more memory bandwidth, double the memory ceiling, and 50% more CPU cores at the top. Since tools like LM Studio and Ollama run on the GPU rather than the Neural Engine, capacity and bandwidth are what matter. Memory capacity decides which models you can load at all, while bandwidth determines how fast they run. If your models fit in 32GB, buy the M6 at $899. If they do not, the M5 Pro is your only option here.

The 2024 models remain worth considering even though Apple has stopped selling them new, with availability via third parties, Apple's refurbished store, or second-hand.

passages.heading: Apple M4
passages.text:
# Apple M4

Benchmarks & Specs

                Last updated: 

            Benchmarks & Specs

With the Apple M4, Apple consolidates its lead in ARM-based desktop and mobile architecture. While the M3 made the jump to the 3 nm process (N3B), the M4 uses the refined second-generation 3 nm manufacturing (N3E). This not only allows higher clock speeds but above all a clearly improved energy efficiency under the same load.

passages.heading: Apple M4
passages.text:
The graphics unit has 10 cores and continues features such as hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading. For gamers and 3D designers in particular, this means realistic lighting calculated in real time, something that was previously unthinkable on an SoC of this size.

A key focus is the Neural Engine (NPU). With 16 cores it reaches a computing power of 38 TOPS (trillion operations per second). This makes the M4 well equipped for local AI workflows and Apple Intelligence.

The**Apple M4** uses LPDDR5X-7500 memory, which results in a bandwidth of 120 GB/s. This is a critical factor for GPU performance and AI workloads, as both benefit greatly from fast data throughput.
